title: Scoped negative result: two-anchor span preservation for P112 decoders
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Scoped proof and independent structural certificate; no new kappa.** A free P112 rectangle with at least two rows and two columns cannot erase a binary direction from any support of a nonzero combination of two coordinate modes. Explicit signed coordinate symmetries certify this for all 28 mode pairs.

Consequently, arbitrary `GL(3,C)` mixing of those two modes and one such correction has at least two replacement terms of COPY rank eight or more. With the other six modes unchanged, the sharp separate COPY sum remains **64**, and the power bill remains at least `8*8^q` for `0<q<=1`. Identity mixing attains it. The statement covers the exactly-two and three active projected-product branches. Singleton-sided rectangles, zero-factor cases, more mixed modes and shared COPY billing are outside scope.

Only `research/p112-multiline-free-rectangles-seed42/` is added. The proof uses finite geometry plus a written argument over arbitrary complex coefficients. No physical supplier, complete recurrence, compiler/hosting/precision admission or multiplication theorem is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- Base: `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983`; refreshed upstream `4040a0f46d67b41c36a472a7cd4af791fd4c36cc` preserves the inputs and accepts the additive patch.
- OS assignment seed **42**, structural decoder track; card `complex-masked-decoder`, **refined** scope. `TASK.json` records three candidates, the single overlap-driven pivot, exact sources and stopping rule.
- The initial one-column idea was released after finding Discussion1434. Its completed [PR1468](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1468), head `5e2d8ec8ebff17c85e813ef1bd6f06312c1fe16a`, covers the complementary singleton-sided case.
- [PR1460](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1460), head `8d53667d9bb09d9b1ffb0f865b5c8dc230eb02f6`, already proves COPY64 for arbitrary nonzero rectangles at pair (4,6). This package adds the stronger per-active-term span lemma, explicit all-pair transport, and a different maximal-erasure check. It does not claim first priority for that COPY64 subcase.
- PR1375 supplies small-rectangle bounds; PR1373 identifies the two-product boundary; PR1331 and PR1432 supply preceding handoffs and fixed-boundary evidence. No pending theorem is assumed. Exact heads are in `TASK.json`.
- The full overlap refresh covered 828 open PRs and 162 discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings; the latest 25 PRs and nearest heads were rechecked before submission. [Claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1316#discussioncomment-18912476).

## Validation

Python 3.12.2, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-multiline-free-rectangles-seed42
```

Expected: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/p112-multiline-free-rectangles-seed42 outcome=negative-result`.

- Primary: all 2,553 nonempty character cuts, 28 symmetry maps, seven Gaussian-rational fixtures / 87,808 entries, 12 controls.
- Separate implementation: all 6,216 two-anchor deletions / 31,080 span identities, 351,232 symmetry pairing entries, one 12,544-entry integer identity, six controls. It imports neither primary nor predecessor code.
- Five external source/receipt corruptions rejected. Both optimized Python 3.14.6 checkers pass in a relocated read-only export with identical file hashes before/after. All 20 research workflow tests pass under Python 3.12.2, as do selected-record integrity, metadata and whitespace checks.

The singleton control disproves a one-anchor extension of the span lemma, not a singleton COPY64 theorem. Omitting compensation changes a constrained entry. No selected cold replay, native admission, proof assistant, independent human review or hosted-CI success is claimed. `VALIDATION.json` binds the checked proof and implementation bytes.

## Open next questions

README/TASK identify two bounded directions: classify three-coordinate support strata before testing `GL(4,C)`, or supply an explicit legal shared-COPY endpoint contract. The former needs new geometry; the latter needs a complete gathering/frame/restoration invoice.
